articles.title: Crock Pot, Ninja, Hamilton Beach and more — these are the best slow cookers for every occasion
articles.summary: I rounded up the best slow cookers, including appliances, including multicookers with searing, from Crock Pot, Hamilton Beach, Ninja and many more.
articles.body: In a world of fancy kitchen tech, the humble slow cooker remains as popular as ever. Many people’s introduction to the appliance is via the “set it and forget it” brand Crock Pot, which is metonymous with the appliance. While the slow cooker is a quite basic appliance, there are still some factors to consider when shopping for one. To find the best highly-rated options, I consulted NBC Selected’s very own shopping experts who are passionate about the slow cookers they use at home. I’m also an active home cook and use my slow cooker often. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best slow cookers and multicookers All of the products below come recommended by NBC Selected staff and/or have at least a four-star average from 500 ratings or more on Amazon, or at least 100 at another major retailer like Walmart or Target. This Crock Pot slow cooker is programmable, so you can customize how you cook your meals beyond basic settings like low, high and warm. It has built-in settings like meal scheduling and customizing cooking style based on the amount of food or the type (like meat or poultry). You can also set it on a timer and cook it for a more precise time using the minutes and the hours, rather than simply timing it yourself. Reviewers say they love how customizable it is and that it’s suitable for feeding large families. NBC Selected video producer Josh Rios also owns the Crock-Pot 6 Quart Cook & Carry Programmable Slow Cooker with Digital Timer, a very similar model from Crock Pot, who received it as a gift and underestimated how much he’d actually end up loving it. After receiving it, “life hit me and this set-it-and-forget-it device has saved my day on so many occasions,” he says. “Being able to make hot delicious meals without having to monitor it is perfect for those who are a little too busy or just want to prepare meals for the long week.” This increasingly popular, do-it-all appliance from Ninja is almost like having 5 different appliances in one. While it has your usual slow cooker features, what sets it apart and makes it a “multicooker” is that it allows you to do the things that would require at least one or more pot, pan or skillet. It has a saute function, so you can prep vegetables like onions before adding in your protein, broth and/or tomato sauces for things like soups and chilis. Plus, it has functions for cooking food sous-vide style, a bake feature and even a proofing feature, which is great for helping yeasted doughs rise before they actually start baking. You can also use it to steam vegetables and fish or braise large pieces of meat. Also worth noting about this appliance is that while slow cookers usually have a stoneware insert, this one has a nonstick pot, so usually it’s slightly easier to clean compared to a ceramic pot. Lastly, it also comes with a kitchen spoon and the insert has handles, so you can transfer it easily from countertop to table. This small and affordable slow cooker from Crock Pot was one of the first appliances I ever bought when I first moved to New York, and it was perfect because my apartment was very small and I didn’t have much room in my cabinets. It has a capacity of 2 quarts, which is the perfect size for making 2 to 3 servings of meals like soup or shredded meat and poultry. It’s also a great size for making appetizers for a small crowd, like queso, buffalo chicken dip or spinach and artichoke dip. You can simply put the insert (which is dishwasher safe) on the dining table and serve with various chips or crudite. I also love that it has small handles on the sides, making it easy to bring to a party. This was the second slow cooker I bought after the one above. I got it because I wanted to start doing more meal prepping to save money and improve my nutrition. I found that the 4-quart capacity is the perfect size for making a week’s worth of meals, including lunches and dinners, which is exactly what I use it for. I’ve used it several times to make things like shredded chicken, pork and steak bites, as well as for chilis, which I love making in the winter time. I usually put everything on low for six to eight hours or on high for at least four hours, and everything is always incredibly tender when the time is up. Plus, the insert and the lid are perfectly dishwasher safe — I’ve put them through one many times and it’s held up very well for over four years. As someone who grew up on the Food Network and previously worked as a contributor at The Pioneer Woman Magazine, I know that home cooks take their Pioneer Woman appliances very seriously. This appliance has regular slow cooker functions like low, high and warm, but it also has more interesting detailing, like multiple handles with wood grain-style detailing. It also has a locking lid, so it’s perfect if you often bring a lot of your meals to potlucks or holiday parties. It has a digital display to show how many hours it has left to cook. Plus, Ree Drummond has many recipes that are meant to be prepared in a slow cooker. I almost always make a few things in the Instant Pot when I visit my family during the holidays, particularly to make meals I don’t often make for myself any other time of the year because I’m so busy, like chili, soup and stews. I love using the Instant Pot’s slow cooker function because, similar to the Ninja Possible Cooker, it has a saute function, so I can use it to soften things like chopped celery and onions before making a pot of soup. Outside of the slow cooker function, it can also make things like grains, yogurt and steamed vegetables. Our Place is an NBC Selected-favorite and several editors on staff, including senior editor Shalwah Evans, reporter Zoe Malin and commerce editor Mili Godio, who have appliances and cookware from the brand. The Dream Cooker is Our Place’s equivalent of the Instant Pot electric pressure cooker — it makes pressure cooking easier and safer than with a traditional appliance because it has a built-in steam release function that doesn’t require using your hands to work. It has a slow cook function so it can make all sorts of meats and proteins tender in hours, but you can also use the pressure cook function to turn those hours into 45 minutes. It also has sear/saute and keep warm functions, and you can even use it to make macaroni and cheese, according to the brand. The insert isn’t dishwasher safe and the brand recommends not using scouring pads to clean. The Beautiful by Drew Barrymore multicooker is similar to the Ninja Possible Cooker, though it’s slightly more affordable and doesn’t have quite as many cooking functions like proofing and baking. NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman-Samuda has this slow cooker and loves its versatility. “I’ve owned a handful of slow cookers over the course of my adult life — including some pretty pricey ones from high-end brands. But I bought this multicooker on a whim last year after seeing a ton of moms in my feed using it and I’ve been blown away by it,” she says. “I love that it has a sear setting so I can brown meats before flipping over to the slow cook setting. It also has a steam setting that is great for cooking frozen dumplings.” Heitman-Samuda also appreciates the fact that the insert is oven-safe (up to 400 degrees Fahrenheit, including the lid) and is suitable for serving out of it on a dining table. How I picked the best slow cookers Here are all the factors and features I considered when making this roundup of slow cooker and multicooking appliances: Features, modes and settings: For the most part, all slow cookers have the baseline functions low, high and keep warm, which is the case for the appliances on this list. With that said, some slow cookers have additional features like a timer and customized cooking settings based on meat and poultry type as well as amount. Plus, a few of the appliances on this list have sear and saute functions which prevent you from having to do any work on a skillet before adding food to the slow cooker. For the list above, I made sure to include appliances with all traditional slow cooker functions, but I also included a few (from Ninja and Our Place, for example), that have additional settings for more multidimensional cooking at home. Size: Common sizes for slow cookers and multicookers range from two to around 8.5 quarts. In the list above, I included appliances that fall within this range and emphasize the benefits of having slow cookers in different sizes and capacities, because each one is great for making different courses of meals or food types, like appetizers and side dishes. Something to keep in mind with large slow cookers, however, is that if you have a small dishwasher, they may be hard to fit and thus might be best if washed by hand (more on this below).Dishwasher safety: Everyone values a little help when it comes to washing dishes, so a dishwasher-safe slow cooker is a major plus. All of the slow cooker inserts and their corresponding lids on the list above, except one, are dishwasher safe according to their brands. Most of the slow cooker inserts are made from dishwasher-safe stoneware and have glass lids (some of which the brands recommend washing on the top rack, which I noted above). The insert for Our Place Dream Cooker, however, isn’t dishwasher safe and best if washed by hand. How to shop for a slow cooker Here are a few things to keep in mind when shopping for a slow cooker. You may benefit from having multiple slow cookers for different purposes and occasions. Decide on the size If you live alone and/or don’t do a ton of meal prep, a slow cooker around 2 to 3 quarts may suffice. If you have a large family that you cook for and/or you rely on a slow cooker to meal prep lunches and dinners, a large capacity appliance is the best way to go. Just keep in mind that if you have a small dishwasher, some inserts may be hard to fit in it, in which case, you may need to wash them by hand. Determine which functions are most important As the roundup above shows, slow cookers have a wide range of features, modes and settings. If you prefer and only want appliances with the usual high, low and keep warm functions, then there’s no need to get a more complex one like the Ninja Possible Cooker. But if you like being able to make many if not most of your meals in the same appliance, then a slow cooker with several functions, like the Instant Pot, for example, are great options. Consider portability and cleaning If you attend a lot of dinner parties and bring food in your slow cooker, then you should consider buying one with a locking lid, which prevents food from leaking or spilling. Plus, some slow cooker inserts are ceramic while others are made from nonstick aluminum, which, depending on what you cook in them, can be harder to clean, so if it isn’t dishwasher safe, this is something to keep in mind. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home and kitchen appliances. I’ve written about the best stainless steel cookware, how to clean cast-iron skillets and I’ve reviewed air fryer toaster ovens. I also previously worked as an editor at several food magazines and sites, and I regularly cook and develop recipes myself at home. For this story, I considered my own culinary expertise and experience, as well as product recommendations from my colleagues who use slow cookers at home. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Ukraine hits Putin's prized bridge in record drone blitz as Kremlin tells lawmakers to prepare for 'victory'
articles.summary: Ukraine struck Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge in what Russia called the war's largest drone attack, setting industrial facilities ablaze.
articles.body: Ukraine launched what Russia described as the largest overnight drone attack of the war Monday, striking President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge and setting industrial facilities ablaze, as separate reports revealed a covert French military mission in Ukraine and preparations in Moscow for a possible return of Russian troops. The developments came days before President Donald Trump is expected to meet Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China, amid renewed U.S.-brokered efforts to end the nearly five-year conflict. "The sheer scale and effectiveness of these drone attacks are remarkable," retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Richard Newton told Fox News Digital. "Ukraine has developed the capability to produce large numbers of drones and strike targets once considered a safe haven deep inside Russia." UKRAINE TARGETS RUSSIA WITH OVER 1,000 DRONES, KILLING 2 AS MOSCOW HOLDS LAST DAY OF ELECTIONS Russia's Defense Ministry claimed its forces intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones across 16 regions, exceeding the previous overnight record of 1,254 on Oct. 29, Reuters reported Nov. 16. The numbers could not be independently verified. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said about 600 drones had been launched toward the capital region since Sunday evening, with 191 intercepted. Russian-installed Crimean governor Sergei Aksyonov confirmed that the Kerch Strait bridge, linking occupied Crimea to mainland Russia, had been struck. The Kremlin characterized the damage as minor. Road traffic was temporarily suspended for repairs, while trains continued running, according to Russian transportation officials. The bridge is both a strategically important supply route and a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014. The strikes also hit Russia's energy sector. Rostov regional governor Yuri Slyusar reported fires at four industrial sites in Azov, where three people were injured. Officials in neighboring Krasnodar said a separate fire broke out at an industrial facility in Ilsky. Falling drone debris reportedly injured six people in the Krasnodar region. ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed Sunday that strikes had disabled more than half of Russia's refining capacity, a figure Fox News Digital could not verify. Two industry sources separately estimated that recent attacks reduced refining capacity by approximately 30%, Reuters reported. "Putin has a serious problem on his hands," Newton said. "Russia is enormous in terms of size; there’s simply no way to 100% defend every refinery, airfield, and military installation." Newton said Ukraine's campaign was designed to strengthen its negotiating position while disrupting Russia's military and logistics networks. "I don’t believe Ukraine has reached a culminating point yet, by any stretch, to change Putin’s mind, but sustained military and economic pressure just may eventually at some point force him to reconsider his position," he said. Secret French military mission In a separate development, Radio France Internationale reported Nov. 16 that French troops had been operating inside Ukraine since at least summer 2026 as part of a confidential mission codenamed "Volia." The mission reportedly consists of small teams making short visits to train Ukrainian personnel and maintain equipment. RFI said French lawmakers had not been informed and alleged that an established French training operation in Poland, known as "Gerfaut," provided a gateway for deployments into Ukraine. An anonymous source familiar with the mission confirmed French personnel's presence to AFP, while stressing that they were not combat troops. "The rotation of French trainers supporting Ukraine in France, Poland, or occasionally in Ukraine is a reality," the source told AFP. "But this is not a military operation. There is absolutely no intention of engaging in coercive actions." France's military general staff did not immediately comment to AFP. The number of troops involved remains unknown. Kremlin reportedly prepares for 'victory' Meanwhile, Russian newspaper Vedomosti reported Nov. 16 that Kremlin officials had instructed lawmakers from Putin's United Russia party to prepare for "victory" and the return of personnel from the battlefield. The message was reportedly delivered during a closed-door seminar attended by senior presidential administration official Sergei Kiriyenko. A source described lawmakers being told to anticipate the possibility of soldiers returning home simultaneously. The report provided no timetable and did not establish that Putin had ordered a withdrawal or decided to end the war. The reports emerged after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi last week resulted in a major prisoner-exchange agreement but no breakthrough over territory. Trump, Putin and Xi were due to meet Thursday, Nov. 19, in Shenzhen, China, with Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov describing the trilateral summit as a potentially significant event. Newton expressed skepticism about an immediate diplomatic breakthrough. "I don't anticipate a major breakthrough on any issue, including Russia's war against Ukraine," he said.
